newsitem.title: USA: Sheridan to take Q4 charge of $17 mln.
newsitem.headline: Sheridan to take Q4 charge of $17 mln.

text.p: Sheridan Healthcare Inc said it expects to take a fourth-quarter charge of $17 million for the sale of 11 offices in the Miami-Fort Lauderdale area.
The company said the charge represents a reduction in the carrying of goodwill and other assets related to the offices -- one of which has already been sold.
As a result of the charge, the company will not show a profit for the fourth quarter, a company spokesman said. He declined to provide specific figures.
The company will report its fourth-quarter earnings near the end of February, he added.
The 11 offices employ about 19 doctors and generated about $15 million in revenue for the quarter ended September 30, the company said.
The company is selling the offices as part of a change in strategy to place more emphasis on its hospital-based business and reduce emphasis on its primary-care business, the spokesman said.

The company's primary-care business, along with its obstetrical and rheumatology businesses, comprise its office-based operations. Its office-based operations account for about 30 percent of the company's yearly revenue, the spokesman said.
